paper.title: Online SuBmodular + SuPermodular (BP) Maximization with Bandit Feedback

settings.name_in_paper: Interactive BP / WS maximization with monolithic feedback (GP contextual bandit)
unmapped: Each round one of m unknown set functions h_q (indexed by context) arrives; the learner adds one item v_t from ground set V to a growing set for that function and observes a noisy marginal gain h_q(v_t|S) + eps_t
Marginal-gain function Delta(phi,S,v) lies in an RKHS with norm <= B
Regret is alpha-regret against alpha * h_q(S_q^*) summed over contexts, with alpha the offline greedy approximation ratio (BP curvature-based or WS submodularity ratio/generalized curvature based)
Items cannot be repeated per function (available action set shrinks)
settings.definition_quote: The optimizer encounters one of $m$ set functions from the set $\{h_1 \ldots h_m \}$ each defined over the finite ground set $V$... The optimizer computes and then performs/plays action $v_{\tvar} \in V$, and then adds $v_\tvar$ to its growing context-dependent set... Monolithic Feedback: The optimizer receives $y_\tvar$ with $y_\tvar = h_{u_\tvar} (v_\tvar| S_{t_{u_\tvar}, u_\tvar}) + \epsilon_\tvar$.

settings.name_in_paper: Interactive BP maximization with separate feedback (known modular lower bound and T_q)
unmapped: Separate noisy marginal-gain feedback for the submodular part f and supermodular part g of a BP function
Learner knows the modular lower bound l_{q,1} of each submodular part
Learner knows the number of items T_q per context
Regret is alpha-regret with alpha = min{1 - kappa_f/e, 1 - kappa^g}
Marginal-gain function lies in an RKHS with norm <= B; items added to a growing set per context
settings.definition_quote: Separate Feedback: In the BP case, pair $(y_{f, \tvar},y_{g, \tvar})$ may be available with $y_{f, \tvar} = f_{u_\tvar} (v_\tvar| S_{t_{u_\tvar}, u_\tvar}) + \epsilon_\tvar/2$ and $y_{g, \tvar} = g_{u_\tvar} (v_\tvar| S_{t_{u_\tvar}, u_\tvar}) + \epsilon_\tvar/2$.

settings.name_in_paper: Interactive BP maximization with separate feedback (unknown modular lower bound, known T_q)
unmapped: Separate noisy marginal-gain feedback for the submodular part f and supermodular part g of a BP function
Learner knows the number of items T_q per context
Regret is alpha-regret with alpha = min{1 - 1/e, 1 - kappa^g}
Marginal-gain function lies in an RKHS with norm <= B; items added to a growing set per context
settings.definition_quote: In certain applications, Assumption (2a) on $l_{q,1}$ may not be reasonable. For these cases, we may modify the algorithm slightly, and provide an alternative bound, that is slightly weaker.

conditions: all h_q are BP functions (monotone submodular + monotone supermodular, normalized)
Delta lies in RKHS with ||Delta||_k <= B (Assumption 1)
tuning: beta_t = sqrt(lambda) B + sqrt(4 log T + log(e + e t/lambda) d_eff)

source.label: thm:bp_regret_bound
source.quote: Let Assumption~\ref{ass:rkhs} hold and assume that $\epsilon_\tvar$ are i.i.d centered sub-Gaussian (i.e., light tailed) noise. Then MNN-UCB (Algorithm~\ref{alg:smucb}) obtains the following regret: (a) When all $h_q$ are BP functions, we have that $\mathbb{E} [\mathcal{R}_{\text{BP}}(\Tvar)] \leq O\left(\sqrt{\Tvar} \left(B \sqrt{\lambda \deff} + \deff\right) \right)$

results.notes: B (RKHS norm bound) mapped to S; d_eff = Tr(K_T(K_T+lambda I)^{-1}). Comparator is alpha times the optimal size-T_q set per context; no single vocabulary comparator fits exactly. Proof invokes Theorem 4.1 of Zenati et al. 2022.

conditions: all h_q are weakly submodular MNN functions with submodularity ratio gamma_q and generalized curvature zeta_q
Delta lies in RKHS with ||Delta||_k <= B (Assumption 1)
tuning: beta_t = sqrt(lambda) B + sqrt(4 log T + log(e + e t/lambda) d_eff)

source.label: thm:bp_regret_bound
source.quote: (b) When all $h_q$ are WS functions, we have that $\mathbb{E} [\mathcal{R}_{\text{WS}}(\Tvar)] \leq O\left(\sqrt{\Tvar} \left(B \sqrt{\lambda \deff} + \deff\right) \right)$

results.notes: WS case of Theorem 1; B mapped to S.

conditions: Assumption 2: modular lower bound l_{q,1} known, separate f/g feedback oracles, T_q known

source.label: thm:bp_regret_bound_dist_strong
source.quote: Let Assumptions~\ref{ass:rkhs} and \ref{ass:separate} hold and assume that $\epsilon_\tvar$ are i.i.d centered sub-Gaussian noise. Then, when all $h_q$ are BP functions, Algorithm~\ref{alg:mnnucb_dist} yields \[ \mathbb{E}[\mathcal{R}_{\text{BP}, 2} (\Tvar)] \leq O\left(\sqrt{\Tvar} \left(B \sqrt{\lambda \deff} + \deff\right) \right) \]

results.notes: B mapped to S. Stronger alpha (distorted greedy baseline).

conditions: Assumptions 2b and 2c: separate f/g feedback, T_q known

source.label: prop:bp_regret_bound_dist_weaker
source.quote: Let Assumption~\ref{ass:rkhs} and \ref{assump:1.2} and \ref{assump:1.3} hold. Additionally, let the conditions on $\epsilon_\tvar$ hold as in Theorem~\ref{thm:bp_regret_bound_dist_strong}. Then Algorithm~\ref{alg:mnnucb_dist} with the modification above yields $\mathbb{E} [\mathcal{R}_{\text{BP, 3}} (\Tvar)] \leq O\left(\sqrt{\Tvar} \left(B \sqrt{\lambda \deff} + \deff\right) \right)$

results.notes: B mapped to S. Weaker alpha, no knowledge of modular lower bound.
